issue_context.title: querystring.stringify does not support BigInt
issue_context.body:
<!--
Thank you for suggesting an idea to make Node.js better.

Please fill in as much of the template below as you're able.
-->

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

```js
> querystring.stringify({a: 12345678901234567n})
'a='
```

it should print `a=12345678901234567`

**Describe the solution you'd like**

support `bigint` in additional to `string`, `number` and `boolean`.

i.e., in [`stringifyPrimitive`](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/39a7f7663e8f70fc774105d8fa41b8e4cc69149f/lib/querystring.js#L158-L166) encode any value where `typeof v  == 'bigint'` as `'' + v`, the same as `'number'`.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

No.
comments: @kennytm what will be the use case of sending such large numbers in bigint form, ideally one will prefer to use string for such cases instead of bigint. Also when the parsing is applied what should be the value of the key, should it be `12345678901234567` or `12345678901234567n` as both are valid options. Can you elaborate on the feature request?

review_comments: I think we should add support in `querystring.parse()` at the same time - it seems impossible to parse it back when you serialize a bigint as a normal number?
I think that'd be less straightforward of a change and is probably better suited for discussion in a separate PR.

@joyeecheung do you mean converting the values of the parsed objects to `number/bigint/string/boolean` because this already returns `true`:
```js
BigInt(querystring.parse(`a=${10n ** 1023n}`).a) === 10n ** 1023n
```
hmm, I see, it'll always be parsed as a string so it's up to the user to decide which numeric type this field should be converted to. In that case nvm.
